sara-cs: Customer (ACME) opened a ticket — embeddings throughput collapsed and started seeing 401s right after a billing sync. They reported vectors/sec dropped ~10x but tokens/sec for text-gen routes looked normal.
sara-cs: Quoting customer: "embed requests returning 401 {\"error\":\"billing_inactive\"} intermittently, and throughput is ~300 vecs/s vs usual ~3k vecs/s."
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2458, paging infra on call.
alex: Looking at logs now — correlate shows their auth calls succeeded, then we started returning 401 from token-validation service around the same time payment webhook retried. Could be short-lived auth cache invalidation.
maria: Also seeing a sharp spike in embed queue depth on region us-east-1: queue_depth metric jumped from 12 -> 110 at the same time. GPU util on pool-embeds-01 hit 99% and stayed there ~2m.
jin: If GPU is saturated with long batches, you will see vectors/sec drop while tokens/sec (from small text-gen) stays stable. Embeds are more sensitive to batch headroom.
alex: Repro plan: try synthetic load focused on embeddings with same request shape. Use k6 to hammer /v1/embeddings with batch sizes matching customer's SDK (~batch=64, dim=1536).
alex: Quick repro command we used:
```
k6 run - <script.js> --vus 200 --duration 3m
// script sends POST /v1/embeddings with 64 inputs each
```
maria: I pulled a sample flamegraph from the runtime at spike time — KV cache locks and batch-merge were hot. We had a routing change earlier that prefers larger batches for cost-savings; looks like policy pushed larger batch formation and coincided with billing webhook causing a transient auth churn.
sara-cs: Customer is blocked, asking for ETA and temporary workaround.
jin: Temporary mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch_bytes / batch_window for that customer route, 2) pin them to a variant with smaller preferred batch targets, or 3) force-fallback to CPU-backed embed variant as emergency.
amber (infra-bot): rollout rollback command executed: `rc rollout revert routing-policy/embeds-batch-agg` — confirmed removed from >50% of traffic.
maria: After rollback, queue depth back to ~15, GPU util dropped to 62%, vectors/sec recovered to ~2.8k for the customer session. No more 401s observed after auth cache TTL bump.
alex: Root cause hypothesis: billing webhook retry briefly marked account as unpaid in auth cache due to race with payment processor -> auth validation failures -> traffic routed/tripped into fallback and batch policy pushed larger batch windows -> GPU saturation and queue head-of-line blocking -> vectors/sec collapse.
samir: Can we add a short-term patch: tolerate billing webhook transient by holding last-known-good status for 30s before flipping account to inactive? Also add alert for vectors/sec drop >50% tied to queue_depth>50.
maria: Filed followup PRs: infrared/patch-embeds-billing-grace (hold 30s) and telemetry/alerts-vecs-queue.
sara-cs: Shared workaround to customer: we rolled back routing and bumped auth cache TTL; please verify on your end and reopen if you still see 401s. Customer confirmed recovery. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Link to graphs: https://observability.company/graphs/INC-2026-2458 (queue_depth, gpu_util, vecs_per_sec)
samir: Next steps: (1) ship billing-grace patch, (2) tighten route QA to avoid batch-policy flips during billing events, (3) add playbook snippet for support to apply per-tenant emergency config. I'll sync with finance on payment webhook reliability.
sara-cs: Thanks team — closing thread once PRs merge and alert is live.
